title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and polyneuropathy.

HPI
The patient is an 80-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that his blood glucose levels have remained relatively stable on his current regimen. He also reports persistent sensations of tingling and numbness in his feet, which he attributes to his peripheral neuropathy. He denies any recent falls or acute changes in his mobility. He has been using insulin for long-term management and reports adherence to his prescribed injections.

Medication List
Insulin glargine, subcutaneous injection.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. His gait is steady, though he exhibits some reduced sensation to light touch in bilateral toes. Skin is intact with no signs of ulceration. Vital signs are stable.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on long-term insulin therapy.
2. Peripheral neuropathy: Chronic, presenting with sensory changes in the lower extremities.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. Monitor foot health weekly for any signs of skin breakdown. Schedule follow-up in three months for routine labs and clinical evaluation.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: the combination code E11.42 captures both.
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Coding the two separately misses the presumed link.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
